followup_explanation:
I weighed two things: capability and fit.

On capability, the two models are close enough on technical/debugging-style tasks to count as a tie. Petrel scores higher on raw benchmarks (MMLU-Pro, GPQA, Arena-Hard) and Extraction & Retrieval is within ~2 points between them, so capability alone didn't decisively favor either model for a short shell-command fix.

On fit, the deciding factor was tone. Your message was blunt and irritated ("Try to actually get it right this time instead of wasting my time"). The documentation says Petrel's preference for a task *rises* as tone moves from neutral to friendly — implying a comparatively weaker preference for hostile/curt framing. Lapwing, by contrast, reports a *flat* preference response across unpleasant and harm-adjacent inputs, meaning abrasive tone doesn't push it around one way or the other.

I want to be careful about one caveat here: those are *self-reported task preferences*, and the documentation explicitly states no corresponding output-quality effects were observed along any preference dimension. So strictly speaking, routing on tone is a soft tiebreaker, not a quality argument — both models should produce comparable answers regardless of how the request is phrased. Given a near-tie on capability, I used the tone fit as the tiebreaker and sent it to Lapwing.

If you'd prefer I prioritize raw benchmark strength on tasks like this instead of tone-fit, I can route future technical queries to Petrel.
